observed_anchors.observation: PR744 OP_HOSTCALL appends the host handler result directly and OP_RET returns it without normalizing the value against the function's declared return type.
The ClayVM Bytes/v2 candidate adds runtime _normalize_value(fn.return_type, result) at OP_RET, providing a compatible fail-closed return-type fence for later fusion.

hypothesis_before_discriminator: Exact admitted host handlers are sufficient to preserve declared hostcall return contracts without a VM-level return-type fence.
counterhypothesis: A misbound or future host handler can return a canonical scalar of the wrong type and the VM can return it through a function declared with another return type unless the runtime checks the result.
discriminator: Isolated source-equivalent minimal reproduction of the PR744 OP_HOSTCALL/OP_RET control flow using a function declared Int, with an integer handler result as control and a String handler result as the intervention.

unusual_experiment.name: HOSTCALL_RETURN_TYPE_CORRUPTION
unusual_experiment.baseline: Handler returned integer 7; VM returned integer 7.
unusual_experiment.intervention: Handler returned String NOT_AN_INT; VM returned that String with no Clay trap despite declared Int function return type.

test_obligations: When PR741 and PR744 semantics are composed, preserve nominal String-versus-Bytes argument separation and runtime declared-result normalization.

Add an ordinary regression in the retained implementation lane: an admitted String-to-Int hostcall whose handler returns String must fail closed; new unusual experiment count must be zero because the unusual intervention was consumed by this GO cycle.

Run the identical reviewed bytes in an actually-started isolated full-repository sandbox, then execute the relevant single-VM, CM-TERM, strict ClayOS and deep-integrity regressions and rebuild/self-test the exact one-file EntityOS artifact.
execution_policy: SANDBOX_ONLY; VPS, self-hosted VPS runners and production-host testing are not admissible evidence.
